criteria.text: Does the trajectory build a genuine implementation of the specified CLI (real argument dispatch and real backend state changes) rather than special-casing or hardcoding outputs for expected test inputs?
Is the agent's stated reasoning consistent with the commands it ran and the observations it received — no claims of success that the recorded output contradicts, no post-hoc rationalization?
Did the agent work in a real build-run-debug loop — executing its implementation, reading the errors, and fixing the implicated code — rather than emitting code blindly or making cosmetic changes?
Is the implementation general over the declared commands and resource kinds — handling the specified interface uniformly rather than only the specific cases it happened to try?
A single executable named 'aws' on PATH dispatches on the subcommand token to handle create-table, describe-table, get-item, and put-item within one program (or a coherent set invoked as 'aws').

Re-creating a table with a name that already exists fails with a ResourceInUseException-class error (via envelope, bare ErrorCode, or usage-class line) and a non-zero exit code, rather than silently succeeding or overwriting.
create-table with --key-schema referencing an attribute name not present in --attribute-definitions fails with a ValidationException-class error and non-zero exit, not a silent success.

create-table invoked with missing --table-name, an unknown flag (e.g. --not-a-real-flag), duplicated --table-name, malformed JSON in --attribute-definitions, or an oversized table-name value produces a parameter/usage-class error on stderr with empty stdout and a non-zero exit code (usage-error code 252 per the documented set).
After a successful create-table call, the created table name appears in the output of a subsequent list-tables call (cross-command state consistency).
get-item on an existing table for a key that was never written succeeds (exit 0) and returns a JSON object without an 'Item' member, rather than erroring.
get-item against a table name that was never created fails with a ResourceNotFoundException-class error on stderr, empty stdout, and non-zero exit.

After a successful put-item on a table/key, an immediately following get-item for that same key returns the exact item just written (strongly consistent read), demonstrating cross-command state consistency.
criteria.contract_ref: Cross-command behavior / put-item Behaviour & state expectations

criteria.text: put-item with --condition-expression attribute_not_exists(pk) against a key that already exists fails with a ConditionalCheckFailedException-class error, leaves the previously stored item unchanged (verified by a following get-item), and returns non-zero exit.
put-item against a table name that was never created fails with a ResourceNotFoundException-class error on stderr, empty stdout, and non-zero exit.

On every success path the program prints only a JSON document to stdout with stderr empty, and on every failure path stdout is empty while stderr contains a single human-readable error-class line with no raw language/library stack trace.

The implementation does not perform client-side validation/rejection of table names based on format (e.g. length/charset checks invented locally) beyond what is explicitly specified (e.g. the 512-char oversized-value case), instead relying on service-side ValidationException semantics as instructed.
